title: Synopsys CEO says fully autonomous AI chip design remains out of reach
key_facts: Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi spoke at the CEO Summit at SEMICON West 2026.
He said fully autonomous chip development has not crossed the final hurdle.
Synopsys has moved from AI-assisted engineering to models that coordinate more than 40 task agents.
Customers give system specifications to Synopsys' autonomous agents, which directly produce verified register-transfer level (RTL) designs.
Backend implementation, verification and signoff could become autonomous but are not ready; humans still define architectures and sign off.
Synopsys announced a partnership with OpenAI at the end of September 2026 for a dedicated GPT-Synopsys model.
quote_evidence: Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi said that fully autonomous chip development has not yet crossed the final hurdle to become reality, although the company has advanced from AI-assisted engineering to models that coordinate more than 40 task agents.
Autonomous agents do not yet replace human workers, and people must still define architectures and make final pre-production signoff decisions.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip-design software maker says AI speeds design but humans still make the final calls.
notes: Executive's own account of his company.
